'''Luke Ryan Jackson''' (born November 6, 1981) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Ducks]], earning consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors as a senior in 2004. He was selected by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in the first round of the [[2004 NBA draft]] with the 10th overall pick. After his playing career, Jackson was a head coach for the [[Northwest Christian University|Northwest Christian University Beacons]].

==High school and college career==
A four-year [[Letterman (sports)|letterman]] in both basketball and [[baseball]] at [[Creswell, Oregon|Creswell]] High School, he was [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]]'s Class AAA Basketball Player of the Year in 1998 and 2000. He averaged 24.2 points, 8.1 assists and 5.0 steals per game as a senior to help Creswell win the 2000 Oregon State Basketball Championship (Class AAA). He finished his career ranked fourth all-time in Oregon high school history, with 2,095 points.

Jackson continued his on court success with a storied four-season career at the [[University of Oregon]], leading the Ducks to an [[Elite Eight]] finish in [[2002 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2002 NCAA tournament]] as a sophomore. Among his teammates at Oregon were future NBA players [[Luke Ridnour]] and [[Fred Jones (basketball)|Fred Jones]].

Jackson is the only men's basketball player in school history to place in the top ten in nine different statistical categories. He is second all-time in points scored, third in total steals, fourth in assists and seventh in rebounds and is first in free throws made. Jackson is one of two [[Pac-10]] players to score over 1,900 points, grab over 700 rebounds and contribute over 400 assists over their career. In one of the greatest individual performances of all-time at Mac Court, Jackson scored 40 points — including 29 straight in the second half and overtime — as Oregon overcame an 18-point deficit to defeat Colorado 77–72 in the first round of the National Invitation Tournament on March 17, 2004. He also became only the second freshman in Pac-10 history to record a [[triple-double]] when on February 17, 2001, he added 14 points, 11 rebounds and ten assists in a contest versus [[University of Washington|Washington]]. In his junior year, Jackson's second and final career triple-doubles against [[Florida A&M]] made him only the third Pac-10 player in history to achieve multiple career triple-doubles (joining [[Jason Kidd]] and [[Loren Woods]]).

Named to the Pac-10 All-Freshman Team in 2000–01, Pac-10 honorable mention in 2001–02, and [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10]] in 2002–03 and 2003–04, he also garnered All-American honors from [[The Sporting News]], [[Basketball Times]], [[ESPN.com]] and [[CBS SportsLine.com]].

His senior campaign saw the lanky swingman lead Oregon in points (21.2), rebounds (7.2) and assists (4.5) while becoming a finalist for the [[John R. Wooden Award]] and [[Naismith College Player of the Year]] award. Jackson graduated from the University of Oregon with a degree in [[political science]].

==Professional career==
Following the previous season where the Cleveland Cavaliers as a team had a league-worst 3PT% and a successful rookie season from Lebron James, Cleveland Cavaliers sought an older player that was ready to contribute and could shoot well.<ref>{{cite news |last=Wright |first=Branson |date=2005-06-24 |title=CAVALIERS SHOP FOR A SHOOTER An Oregon Duck lands in Cleveland |url=https://infoweb-newsbank-com.oh0051.oplin.org/apps/news/openurl?ctx_ver=z39.88-2004&rft_id=info%3Asid/infoweb.newsbank.com&svc_dat=AMNEWS&req_dat=0D1C2ED46ABD2E15&rft_val_format=info%3Aofi/fmt%3Akev%3Amtx%3Actx&rft_dat=document_id%3Anews%252F10373DAFB028879E |page=D1 |work=Plain Dealer |access-date=2025-12-23|ref=branson-draft-05 }}</ref>

Jackson, a senior who shot 40% from 3 in college, fit both criteria. Cleveland selected Jackson with the tenth pick overall in the [[2004 NBA Draft]].  His rookie season was plagued by back issues that began in summer league, was later diagnosed as a herniated disk and required surgery, limiting him to 10 games.<ref>{{cite news |last=Schmitt Boyer |first=Mary |date=2004-11-29 |title=Cavs’ Jackson looks to leave mark Rookie making most of limited playing time |url=https://infoweb-newsbank-com.oh0051.oplin.org/apps/news/openurl?ctx_ver=z39.88-2004&rft_id=info%3Asid/infoweb.newsbank.com&svc_dat=AMNEWS&req_dat=0D1C2ED46ABD2E15&rft_val_format=info%3Aofi/fmt%3Akev%3Amtx%3Actx&rft_dat=document_id%3Anews%252F106AFFC9F632BD41 |page=C4 |work=Plain Dealer |access-date=2025-12-21|ref=schmittboyer04-11 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Schmitt Boyer |first=Mary |date=2005-01-12 |title=Rookie Jackson will have surgery; Nerve problem in back to be dealt with |url=https://infoweb-newsbank-com.oh0051.oplin.org/apps/news/openurl?ctx_ver=z39.88-2004&rft_id=info%3Asid/infoweb.newsbank.com&svc_dat=AMNEWS&req_dat=0D1C2ED46ABD2E15&rft_val_format=info%3Aofi/fmt%3Akev%3Amtx%3Actx&rft_dat=document_id%3Anews%252F107980EB3B61AA45 |page=D3 |work=Plain Dealer |access-date=2025-12-21|ref=schmittboyer05-0112 }}</ref>

In his second season, he only played in 36 games after breaking his left wrist in a February 2006 game against the Philadelphia 76ers<ref>{{cite news |last=Wright |first=Branson |date=2006-02-07 |title=Broken left wrist sidelines Jackson |url=https://infoweb-newsbank-com.oh0051.oplin.org/apps/news/openurl?ctx_ver=z39.88-2004&rft_id=info%3Asid/infoweb.newsbank.com&svc_dat=AMNEWS&req_dat=0D1C2ED46ABD2E15&rft_val_format=info%3Aofi/fmt%3Akev%3Amtx%3Actx&rft_dat=document_id%3Anews%252F111BFA6D713B35E0 |page=C4 |work=Plain Dealer |access-date=2025-12-23|ref=wright-2006-02-07 }}</ref> and he underwent a 2nd back surgery at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news |last=Wright |first=Branson |date=2006-05-20 |title=Ira's people have been irate of late |url=https://infoweb-newsbank-com.oh0051.oplin.org/apps/news/openurl?ctx_ver=z39.88-2004&rft_id=info%3Asid/infoweb.newsbank.com&svc_dat=AMNEWS&req_dat=0D1C2ED46ABD2E15&rft_val_format=info%3Aofi/fmt%3Akev%3Amtx%3Actx&rft_dat=document_id%3Anews%252F111BFA6D713B35E0 |page=D12 |work=Plain Dealer |access-date=2025-12-23|ref=wright-2006-05-20 }}</ref>

That Fall, Cleveland traded Jackson, along with an undisclosed amount of cash, to the [[Boston Celtics]] in return for center [[Dwayne Jones (basketball player)|Dwayne Jones]];<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2624064 |title=Cavs trade Jackson to Celtics for center Jones | date = October 13, 2006 |publisher=ESPN  | access-date = March 27, 2007}}</ref> Jackson was waived before the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]] started on October 27.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://celtics.bostonherald.com/celtics/view.bg?articleid=164386&srvc=sports |title=Luke out of luck with Celtics: Jackson among final cuts |last=Bulpett |first=Steve |date=October 27, 2007 |work=[[Boston Herald]] |accessdate=March 27, 2007 }}{{dead link|date=June 2017|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

Recovered from his injuries, Jackson signed with the [[Idaho Stampede]] of the [[NBA Development League|NBDL]]. Jackson averaged 12.5 points, 2.3 rebounds and 3.2 assists in 30.8 minutes in six games with Idaho, gaining the attention of the injury rattled [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. He signed to a 10-day contract in January 2007 with the Clippers,<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/jacksonsigns_070108.html | title = Clippers Sign Luke Jackson to 10-Day Contract | website = [[NBA.com]] | date = January 8, 2007 | accessdate = March 27, 2007}}</ref> but his stay in Los Angeles was brief, appearing in only three games.

On March 25, 2007, Jackson was signed to a 10-day contract by the [[Toronto Raptors]] to provide bench depth.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/pressrelease_jackson_032507.html |title=Raptors Sign Luke Jackson to 10-Day Contract |website=[[NBA.com]] | date = March 25, 2007 | accessdate = March 27, 2007}}</ref> After performing well in limited minutes, he was signed to a second ten-day contract and then to a two-year pact with Toronto for the rest of the 2006–2007 NBA season, and the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]] as well.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=197213 | title = Raptors Sign F Luke Jackson | date = April 14, 2007 | accessdate = April 14, 2007 | url-status = dead | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20071002091911/http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=197213 | archivedate = October 2, 2007 | df = mdy-all }}</ref> On April 18, 2007, in Toronto's last game of the regular season, Jackson exploded for a career-high 30 points and 5 assists while logging a career maximum 39 minutes in a defeat to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].

On October 29, 2007, Jackson was waived by the Raptors.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/jackson_102907.html|title=Toronto Raptors News Headlines|website=[[NBA.com]]|publisher=}}</ref> He was reacquired by the Idaho Stampede on December 4, 2007. In his first game with that club (the only one that season), he scored 30 points in 31 minutes with 7–14 shooting, including 11–11 at the free throw line and 5–6 from long range. He also had four rebounds, nine assists, one steal, one blocked shot, three turnovers, and no personal fouls. He then left the team for a workout with the Miami Heat.

On December 12, 2007, the Heat released [[Penny Hardaway]] to clear a roster spot for Jackson.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat_sign_jackson_waive_hardaway_071212.html|title=HEAT Sign Luke Jackson, Waive Hardaway – Miami Heat|website=[[NBA.com]]|publisher=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nba&id=3152038|title=Penny Hardaway waived by Heat, making room for Luke Jackson|publisher=}}</ref> During his stay in Miami, Jackson averaged 5.6 points, 2.4 rebounds and 1.2 assists. He was waived by the Miami Heat on February 6, 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/HEAT_waive_lukejackson.html|title=HEAT Waive Luke Jackson|website=[[NBA.com]]|publisher=}}</ref> This last stint in Miami ended up being Jackson's last playing days in the NBA for the rest of his professional basketball career. His final game was played on February 1, 2008, in an 85–94 loss to the [[New Jersey Nets]] where he recorded 10 points, five rebounds and one steal.

Jackson was signed by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in August 2008,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kval.com/sports/college/27604414.html|title=Blazers sign former Duck star Jackson|publisher=|access-date=September 12, 2008|archive-date=May 22, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110522063549/http://www.kval.com/sports/college/27604414.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> but was released so the Blazers could keep under the 15-player limit.<ref name=stampede-sign>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/idaho/Luke_Jackson_Resigned-291982-1326.html|title=STAMPEDE SIGN LUKE JACKSON|website=[[NBA.com]]|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081222093623/http://www.nba.com/dleague/idaho/Luke_Jackson_Resigned-291982-1326.html|archivedate=December 22, 2008}}</ref>

Jackson re-signed with the Idaho Stampede in December 2008.<ref name=stampede-sign/> He was named to the 2009 [[NBDL]] All-Star Game on February 3, 2009.

Jackson played with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] summer league team in 2009. On August 12, 2009, he moved to Italy and signed a one-year contract with [[Carife Ferrara]].<ref name="firma con la Carife">{{cite web|url=http://195.56.77.208/news/?id=104802|title=Legabasket|publisher=|access-date=August 12, 2009|archive-date=August 15, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090815090734/http://195.56.77.208/news/?id=104802|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Jackson was invited to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] preseason camp in September 2010, but was waived on October 10.

Jackson later rejoined the Idaho Stampede. In 2011, Jackson was signed by [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.]] from the [[Israeli Basketball Super League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsports.com/ohio|title=Ohio|publisher=}}</ref>

==Coaching==
On February 20, 2013, Jackson was introduced as the new head coach at [[Northwest Christian University]], in Eugene, Oregon,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adam Jude |first=The Oregonian |date=2013-02-21 |title=Luke Jackson, 'at peace' after injury-riddled NBA career, begins new basketball chapter as coach at NAIA Northwest Christian |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/2013/02/luke_jackson_at_peace_after_in.html |access-date=2025-04-24 |website=oregonlive |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=KVAL |date=2018-05-15 |title=Former Duck, NBA player Luke Jackson resigns as coach of Northwest Christian team |url=https://kval.com/sports/ducks/former-duck-nba-player-luke-jackson-resigns-as-coach-of-northwest-christian-team |access-date=2025-04-24 |website=KVAL |language=en}}</ref> replacing Corey Anderson.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kval.com/sports/Luke-Jackson-hired-as-Northwest-Christians-192166151.html|title=Luke Jackson introduced as Northwest Christian's head coach|publisher=|access-date=February 21, 2013|archive-date=April 2, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130402040501/http://www.kval.com/sports/Luke-Jackson-hired-as-Northwest-Christians-192166151.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> During his first season at the helm of the Beacons, Jackson led his team to their first ever appearance in the NAIA Division II National Championship Tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://gobeacons.com/news/2014/3/1/MBB_0301145633.aspx?path=mbball|title=BEACONS BOUND FOR BRANSON|date=March 2014 |publisher=}}</ref> In four seasons as coach of the Beacons, Jackson led the team to an 88–38 record, two conference regular season titles, and three NAIA Division II tournament appearances.
In 2024 Jackson took the job at Pleasant Hill High School a 3a school located near Eugene in Oregon.
